item.title: Flying Fijians ready to rumble in Pacific Nations Cup final
item.description: FIJI Water Flying Fijians interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula says Japan’s players are genetically fast and agile, and they are well aware of the challenges they will face during the final of the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup tonight. Seruvakula says the Flying Fijians will look to build long, constructive phases with ball in hand in an effort to test and eventually wear down the Japanese defe
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Water Flying Fijians interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula says Japan’s players are genetically fast and agile, and they are well aware of the challenges they will face during the final of the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup tonight.

Seruvakula says the Flying Fijians will look to build long, constructive phases with ball in hand in an effort to test and eventually wear down the Japanese defence.

He says discipline will also be a key factor for Fiji as they look to execute their game plan and maintain pressure throughout the match.

Flying Fijians Captain Tevita Ikanivere says the players have prepared well and are ready for Japan.

Seruvakula says they have played Japan before and they know what to do to counter them.

Fiji will play Japan in the final of the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup at 10.05pm today.

Canada will face USA for the third place playoff at 9pm tonight.

item.title: 10-year-old taken to hospital after squishy toy bursts in his face
item.description: A family day at the Royal Adelaide Show ended with Mason, the ten-year-old boy being taken to hospital after his mother says an unknown substance from the toy entered his eyes, ears, nose and mouth. Mason was playing with the toy at a stall on Friday when it suddenly burst.
item.content:encoded:
A family day at the Royal Adelaide Show ended with Mason, the ten-year-old boy being taken to hospital after his mother says an unknown substance from the toy entered his eyes, ears, nose and mouth.

Mason was playing with the toy at a stall on Friday when it suddenly burst.

His mother Amanda says her son began coughing, choking and struggling to breathe after the substance sprayed onto his face.

Mason was taken to hospital for treatment following the incident.

Amanda says her son continued coughing after leaving hospital and was later taken back for X-rays amid concerns that some of the substance may have entered his lungs.

She says one of her biggest concerns is not knowing what was inside the toy.

Amanda claims the stall owner was unable to provide packaging or a product code that could help identify the toy and its contents.

Concerns have also been raised that the toy may have been a counterfeit version, although this has not been confirmed.

Amanda is warning other parents to be cautious with similar toys and is calling for stronger controls to help prevent another child from being hurt.

The Consumer Council of Fiji has shared the incident as a warning to parents in Fiji to be cautious with squishy toys.

item.title: Best crop farmer urges young people to take up commercial farming
item.description: Young people are being urged to return to the villages and take up commercial farming, with this year’s Best Farmer in the Crop Category, Devendra Singh, saying farming can provide a good source of income while making productive use of Fiji’s land. Singh says farming can provide a good source of income while making productive use of Fiji’s land.
item.content:encoded:
Young people are being urged to return to the villages and take up commercial farming, with this year’s Best Farmer in the Crop Category, Devendra Singh, saying farming can provide a good source of income while making productive use of Fiji’s land.

Singh says farming can provide a good source of income while making productive use of Fiji’s land.

He currently farms on two leased properties, with more than 3,000 yaqona plants. His goal is to increase that number to more than 10,000 in the coming years.

Singh says he earns between $300,000 and $400,000 per year.

He says farming is not difficult if people work hard and manage their farms properly, adding that it can provide a good income.

Singh says his farming journey has not always been easy sharing his farm was badly affected by yaqona dieback disease a few years ago, but he replanted and continued farming.

He says he has also encouraged young people who come to him for grog to consider growing yaqona themselves.

Singh says instead of only drinking grog, young people should start farming yaqona, adding that many of them have now taken up farming.

Singh is also calling on Government officials and agricultural extension officers to spend more time in villages, meet with Turaga-ni-Koro and mataqali, and discuss how land can be better used for farming.

He says even dry and hilly land can be productive, with opportunities to grow vegetables, raise livestock and plant crops such as watermelons.

Singh says farmers continue to face challenges, including poor road access and yaqona theft.

He says it took him up to four hours a day to reach his farm by horse because of poor road conditions.

Singh is also calling on the media to highlight the practice of buying green yaqona and is urging the Government to stop people from selling green yaqona.

He is encouraging young people to work hard, make productive use of available land and view commercial farming as a reliable source of income.

item.title: Kishore family gets a taste of America in Suva
item.description: Kishore says the event offered something different for families, with American football, basketball, food and live entertainment among the activities on offer. He says despite some rain, the atmosphere remained lively as people continued to arrive and take part in the activities.
item.content:encoded:
Kishore says the event offered something different for families, with American football, basketball, food and live entertainment among the activities on offer.

He says despite some rain, the atmosphere remained lively as people continued to arrive and take part in the activities.

For Kishore, another highlight was seeing people from different cultures and backgrounds coming together and enjoying the event.

He says the variety of sports, food and entertainment made the showcase an enjoyable experience for his family while also giving them an opportunity to learn more about American culture.

Kishore says he would like to see more events like the American Showcase organised in Fiji, giving families opportunities to spend time together while experiencing different cultures and activities.

item.title: Savusavu residents to raise climate concerns directly with Kamikamica at FMA Town Hall
item.description: Savusavu residents will have the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he will attend the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues next Wednesday. The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum will be held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu from 7pm to 9.30pm on 23rd September.
item.content:encoded:
Savusavu residents will have the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he will attend the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues next Wednesday.

The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum will be held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu from 7pm to 9.30pm on 23rd September.

The forum, organised by the FMA, will give residents an opportunity to raise concerns about environmental and climate challenges affecting their communities, question Government action and propose practical solutions.

Kamikamica will be joined by Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Environment Dr Sivendra Michael, other Government officials and experts from regional agencies who will be in Savusavu for the PINA Media Summit.

The discussion will be moderated by fijivillage News Director Vijay Narayan and Fiji Television Manager News Stella Taoi.

Residents are encouraged to share their own experiences, including changes they have observed, challenges affecting their livelihoods and solutions they believe should receive greater attention.

Questions around Government responses and the support needed by communities will also form part of the discussion.

The forum will be livestreamed across participating media platforms, including fijivillage.

It will be held alongside the 8th Pacific Media Summit, hosted by the Fijian Media Association and the Pacific Islands News Association.

The town hall is aimed at bringing community voices into the regional gathering of Pacific journalists and media leaders, while creating a direct platform for public discussion and accountability on climate and environmental issues.

The event is supported by PACMAS and forms part of the Fijian Media Association’s collaborative town hall initiative involving Fiji’s media organisations.

Residents of Savusavu and surrounding communities are being invited to attend and take part in the discussion.

item.title: Young Taveuni inmates gain skills to prepare for life after release
item.description: A four-day Seeds of Success training programme concluded at the facility yesterday, with Minister for Youth and Sports Jese Saukuru encouraging participants to use the opportunity to prepare for their return to their families and communities. The programme is being delivered through a partnership between the Ministry of Youth and Sports and the Fiji Corrections Service.
item.content:encoded:
A four-day Seeds of Success training programme concluded at the facility yesterday, with Minister for Youth and Sports Jese Saukuru encouraging participants to use the opportunity to prepare for their return to their families and communities.

The programme is being delivered through a partnership between the Ministry of Youth and Sports and the Fiji Corrections Service.

It focuses on equipping young inmates with practical skills, confidence and knowledge that could assist them in finding employment or pursuing business opportunities after their release.

Saukuru told participants that their past mistakes do not have to determine their future and encouraged them to remain positive and make use of the opportunities available to them.

He says providing young inmates with the right skills can better prepare them for employment, entrepreneurship and their return to their communities.

Saukuru says the Ministry plans to continue taking training programmes into correctional facilities, to help prepare young people before they are released .

He says the Ministry also remains ready to support young people as they work towards rebuilding their lives and making a positive contribution to their communities.

item.title: Cultural events help people understand each other- Jeremy Paul
item.description: Manava Performing Arts dancer Jeremy Paul says it was exciting for the group to perform at the event as part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of the United States. Paul says the atmosphere was lively, with children, young people and older members of the community coming together to enjoy the music, performances and other activities.
item.content:encoded:
Manava Performing Arts dancer Jeremy Paul says it was exciting for the group to perform at the event as part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of the United States.

Paul says the atmosphere was lively, with children, young people and older members of the community coming together to enjoy the music, performances and other activities.

He says it was also good to see people taking time out to relax, have fun and enjoy the event together.

Beyond the entertainment, Paul says events such as the American Showcase give Fijians an opportunity to learn more about other cultures.

He says Fiji is a multicultural country, and experiencing another country’s music, food, fashion and traditions can help people better understand different cultures.

Paul says there is often more to a culture than what people may see or know from the outside, and events such as the American Showcase allow people to experience some of those traditions for themselves.
